claim: How evenly a model satisfies the individual instructions in a prompt, and how evenly it satisfies them in pairs, predicts whether it satisfies all of them at once, beyond its average per-instruction accuracy. Supported only if, among groups of responses to multi-instruction prompts that are matched on per-instruction accuracy, both the variance of per-instruction satisfaction rates and the variance of pairwise co-satisfaction rates decrease monotonically as the all-instructions-satisfied rate rises; and if during training the method with the lowest values of both variances also has the highest prompt-level accuracy.

experiments: Define the diagnostics. Setup: for a prompt with N instructions and K sampled responses, record which responses satisfy which instruction; VIA is the variance across instructions of the per-instruction satisfaction rate; VSA is the variance across instruction pairs of joint satisfaction divided by the smaller of the two individual rates (pairs with a zero rate excluded). Motivation: GRPO with a count reward on IFTrain makes Qwen3-1.7B improve reliably on instruction types it already does well, while gains on medium and hard types vary widely and types with very low starting accuracy barely improve.

Relate the diagnostics to all-pass accuracy at fixed instruction accuracy. Setup: AdvancedIF test prompts; pool responses from 15 models (GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, GPT-5, GPT-4o, GPT-OSS-120B and 20B, several Qwen 3 and 3.5, Olmo 3 and Llama 3 sizes); repeatedly sample groups of 128 responses whose instruction accuracy is 0.68 +- 0.01 (the models' mean) and compute VIA, VSA and prompt-level accuracy. Result: both VIA and VSA show a consistent inverse relationship with prompt accuracy (shown in a figure; no correlation coefficient reported).

Track training dynamics. Setup: per-prompt VIA, VSA, instruction coverage (share of instructions satisfied by at least one response in the group), prompt accuracy and policy entropy over RL steps for count reward, warm start plus count reward, and warm start plus scarcity reward. Result: warm-started runs start with higher coverage and prompt accuracy; the full method lowers VIA and VSA fastest and furthest and keeps policy entropy higher, while the count-reward baseline's entropy collapses (figures only).
